questions.question: Why does the vision encoder produce tokens that the text decoder cannot consume directly?
options: Image tokens live in a basis the encoder learned during vision pretraining with no correspondence to the decoder's word vectors
They are in a different file format
questions.explanation: The two encoders learn independent bases; a bridge module is required to align them in a shared space.

questions.question: What non-linearity sits between MLPProjector.fc1 and fc2?
options: No activation; the projector is two linear layers in series
questions.explanation: MLPProjector.forward computes fc2(F.gelu(fc1(x))). The GELU gives the two linear projections a nonlinear middle stage.

questions.question: After train() freezes the vision encoder and MockTextEmbedding, which parameters are optimized?
options: All encoder, text-table, and projector parameters
Only MLPProjector parameters; the encoder and text table have requires_grad=False
No parameters, because Adam cannot optimize a frozen module
questions.explanation: train() calls freeze on the encoder and text module, then constructs Adam with projector.parameters(). The projector is the only trainable bridge in this fixture.

questions.question: What does cosine_alignment_loss(image_emb, text_emb) return when the two vectors point in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Loss is 1 - cos(angle). Antiparallel vectors have cos = -1, so the loss is 1 - (-1) = 2.0.

questions.question: Why does CLS pooling get used to produce a single image-level vector from 197 tokens?
options: Captions are one vector per sample so the image side also needs one vector; the CLS token is the encoder's built-in image summary
questions.explanation: Alignment is one image vector against one caption vector; CLS pooling produces that image vector with no extra parameters.

questions.question: With the default AlignConfig, what dimensional map does MLPProjector implement?
questions.explanation: AlignConfig sets vision_hidden=768, projection_hidden=1024, and text_hidden=512. Those values become the input, hidden, and output widths of the two linear layers.
